summary: Nora's ambient deciders can now see each other's verdicts. A shared decision log records every gate verdict, participation determination, proactive decision and tag outcome, and the participation turn and the proactive pass each read the others' rows for their whole workspace.
details: Issue #199: the Relevance Gate persisted nothing durable (metrics and trace attributes only), the proactive adaptor logged only its own reminder rows, and the determination log was written and read back into no prompt. Measured on 2026-09-10 — participation answered a question at 16:43, the tag turn one second later re-derived the whole answer and died, and the proactive decider raised the same question in another room at 18:03.

A new `decision_log` table (migration 0053), append-only, with one row per decision: which decider, which room, the verdict, a short clause of its own reasoning, and when. Five writers: the participation trigger on every gate verdict (including the no_go verdicts nothing downstream can see, and carrying the error kind when one failed closed, so «the gate said no» and «the gate was down» stay apart); the fire path on every participation and proactive act determination; the proactive decide turn on every decision including its declines; and the tag path on every turn, including the ones that said nothing.

Two readers, each excluding its own writer — a decider reading back its own last verdict is a decider agreeing with itself. The participation turn's prompt gains a `<loop_decisions>` block carrying what her proactive half already raised; the proactive decide turn's prompt gains one carrying the gate, participation and tag rows. Both are scoped to the WORKSPACE, not the room, and that is what makes the log answer the incident at all: a proactive row fires into the workspace's home room and nowhere else, while the thread it is about runs wherever the group is talking — on 2026-09-10 those were different rooms on different platforms, so a room-scoped read would have seen nothing. Bounded at 20 rows over 24 hours, with an age on every row.

The Relevance Gate neither writes nor reads it, deliberately. Its whole shape is one call, transcript plus standing, no tools and no loop; a writer with a fail-soft path is not that, and design 36 §6 forbids it seeing what she has already raised, because a pending proactive row carries a note title. Its verdict is still durable, recorded one layer out by the trigger that called it.

No speech, no title and no person identifier reaches a row or a render. A row carries a code-derived label — a fail-closed error kind, a determination's disposition — and never model text; the decide turn's own `why` is deliberately not stored, because it is written about a note and would carry note titles into a block whose own note says it holds no notes. A note appears as its id, which the participation turn resolves against the `<notes>` block it already has. A room appears under its operator-authored policy label or not at all.

A row is written at turn COMPLETION — after the message went out, or after the decision to stay silent was taken. That is what closes the sequential duplicate: the send at 16:43:57 is durable before the tag turn at 16:44:04 reads anything.
limitations: The tag turn WRITES but does not READ: a tag one second behind a participation answer still re-derives it. That read is a separate, smaller change (it needs a 10-minute window rather than 24 hours) and is not in this branch.

Every writer and both reads are fail-soft and bounded on a 2-second wall clock: a decision log that is down costs a thinner prompt and a counter (`nora_errors_total{stage="decision_log_read"}` / `{stage="decision_log_write"}`), never a dropped reply — so a silently degraded log reads as a quiet estate unless those series are watched.

Whether the blocks actually change either decider's verdicts is unmeasured. The Relevance Gate suite grades a prompt this change does not touch; the proactive decide suite grades one it does, and it has not been run against this change.

The log closes the SEQUENTIAL duplicate, not the concurrent one. A tag that lands while a participation turn is still running reads a log that does not yet contain it, and both turns answer; serialising that is `ConversationSlots`' job, and this is a record rather than a lock.
